about: Topic items that make sure every 'hold in head' and 'must verify' entry of docs/research/round5/expert/E2_domain_targets.json is taught. 'items' are merged by build_curriculum.py into curriculum.json (app -> module -> items; extra fields 'he', 'domain' and 'src' stay here). 'pending' items wait for a planned new module (docs/research/round7/mapping/); the build skips them. 'covered' records where each other entry is already taught. Coverage table: docs/research/round7/mapping/E2_COVERAGE.md.

M0.1.n: About 30 anchor results reproduced on paper in minutes
M0.1.teach: Anchor-results list: about 30 results across linear algebra, probability, optimization and numerics (SVD, projection, condition number, LLN/CLT, KKT, stability regions, ...) that the learner re-derives on paper in minutes; each later math module adds its anchors to the list, and timed paper-only recall drills (no tools) recur through the course.
M0.1.he: כ-30 תוצאות עוגן שהוא משחזר על נייר בדקות

M6.11.n: Every result two ways (analytic vs numeric, or two independent agents)
M6.11.teach: Two-route verification as a standing protocol: derive analytically, then check with an independent numeric route (Monte Carlo, finite differences, a second solver) or a second independently prompted agent; agree to a stated tolerance before trusting the result, and record which route was wrong when they disagree.
M6.11.he: כל תוצאה בשתי דרכים: אנליטית מול נומרית, או שני סוכנים בלתי תלויים

M9.9.teach: Wave impedance: eta = sqrt(mu/epsilon), 377 ohm in free space, impedance of a dielectric or lossy medium; E/H ratio of a plane wave; reflection at an impedance step and the analogy to a transmission line (bridge to circuit impedance in M11.1 and to the RF module).

M3.2.teach: Limiting-case checks as a habit: test every derived formula at its limits before use (driven damped oscillator at omega->0, omega->infinity, gamma->0; Q->infinity), and recognize which limit a wrong sign or factor would violate.

M11.13.teach: Model-versus-measurement comparison: write the prediction with its uncertainty before measuring, compare residuals with the combined (GUM) uncertainty, and read a disagreement as information about the model, the instrument or the setup.

M11.13.n: Measurement (scope, NanoVNA, spectrum analyzer) vs SPICE
M11.13.teach: Bench-versus-SPICE loop: simulate first, then measure with oscilloscope, NanoVNA and spectrum analyzer; explain each discrepancy (probe loading and ground lead, parasitics, component tolerance, instrument bandwidth and RBW).
M11.13.he: מדידה (סקופ, NanoVNA, מנתח ספקטרום) מול SPICE

M7.4.teach: Integration (processing) gain: coherent summation of N samples raises SNR by 10log10(N) dB when the signal is coherent and the noise white; non-coherent integration gains less; how the gain appears in an FFT bin and in a matched filter, and when correlated noise or phase drift breaks it.

Constant false alarm rate detection: why a fixed threshold fails when the noise level is unknown, cell-averaging CFAR (reference and guard cells, threshold multiplier for a design Pfa), CFAR loss, and behavior at clutter edges and with multiple targets.

M4.6.n: Golden test vectors (known tone + noise: SNR out = SNR in + gain)
M4.6.teach: Golden test vectors: synthesize a known tone in white noise at a known SNR, run it through the processing chain (window, FFT, filter) and check the output SNR equals input SNR plus the predicted gain minus window loss; keep the vectors as a regression suite.
M4.6.he: חבילת וקטורי בדיקה זהובים (טון ידוע + רעש: SNR יוצא = SNR נכנס + רווח)

M4.10.n: Comparison with GNU Radio or MATLAB
M4.10.teach: Cross-tool verification: reproduce a filter or spectrum result in a second independent tool (NumPy/SciPy vs MATLAB or GNU Radio) and compare to a tolerance; typical sources of disagreement are scaling and normalization conventions, window definitions and one- vs two-sided spectra.

M4.8.teach: Working with real recorded IQ data: file formats and metadata, sample-rate and frequency offsets, DC offset and IQ imbalance, gain calibration; a processing chain is accepted only after it works on recordings, not only on synthetic data.

M5.6.teach: Monte Carlo evaluation of an estimator against known truth: N runs with simulated truth, RMSE versus the filter-reported sigma and versus the Cramer-Rao bound, number of runs needed for a stated confidence.
Jacobian check for EKF and linearization: compare the analytic or symbolic Jacobian with central finite differences, choose the step size, and flag entries whose relative error exceeds a tolerance.

M23.4.teach: Coding gain read off a BER/BLER curve: dB saved at a target error rate versus uncoded modulation, the waterfall region, the gap to capacity at the code rate, and what decoding latency and complexity buy it.

M23.2.teach: Synchronization in a digital receiver: carrier frequency and phase recovery, symbol timing recovery, frame synchronization with preambles; the effect of residual frequency offset and timing error on the constellation and the BER.
SDR cable loopback: transmitter to receiver through attenuators (never over the air), set a known SNR, measure BER and EVM and compare with theory; account for phase noise and IQ imbalance.

M23.6.n: BER vs theory in AWGN and Rayleigh
M23.6.teach: Monte Carlo BER simulation checked against closed forms: BPSK in AWGN Q(sqrt(2Eb/N0)) and in Rayleigh fading about 1/(4 SNR) at high SNR; how many bit errors are needed for a confident estimate.

M11.7.teach: Friis cascade of noise factors F = F1 + (F2-1)/G1 + (F3-1)/(G1G2) + ...: why the LNA goes first, the cost of cable loss before it, equivalent noise temperature, and sensitivity in dBm from kTB, NF and required SNR.

M11.10.teach: First-article inspection checklist for a new board: visual and continuity checks, current-limited first power-up, rail voltages and ripple, thermal scan, functional and parametric tests against the specification, and a written record.

M12.10.teach: Efficiency chain from source to output: battery or generator, converter, motor, gearbox, propeller or load; multiply stage efficiencies, find where losses become heat, and size the source for the delivered power.

M13.19.teach: N-1 security criterion: the grid must stay within limits after the loss of any single element; contingency analysis with power flow, and why N-1 does not cover common-mode or cascading failures.
Verification on standard test systems: solve the IEEE 14-bus power flow and compare voltages and flows with the published solution before trusting a power-flow code.

M12.8.n: Thrust and current measurement of a drone motor
M12.8.teach: Thrust-stand measurement of a brushless drone motor with propeller: thrust, voltage, current and RPM; compare with the Kt/Kv motor model and the actuator-disk hover-power estimate.
M12.8.he: מדידת דחף וזרם של מנוע רחפן

M14.2.teach: Thermal measurement against a thermal-resistance model: thermocouples, thermistors and IR cameras (emissivity and reflections), sensor placement and contact errors, and comparing measured temperature rise with the predicted R_th times power.

M15.12.teach: Checking performance predictions against flight logs (ArduPilot/PX4 logs or published flight-test data): fit a drag polar from logged power and speed, and compare range and endurance with the Breguet estimates.

M17.5.teach: Splits that respect the data's structure: hold out by time, by sensor or platform and by site; grouped cross-validation; why random splits leak correlated samples and overstate accuracy.
M17.5.domain: ENG · Machine learning and deep learning

M17.5.teach: Simple baselines first: majority class, linear or logistic model, nearest neighbor, and the classical non-learned detector; report the deep model's margin over the best baseline, with its uncertainty.
M17.5.domain: ENG · Machine learning and deep learning

M17.5.teach: Ablation studies: remove or replace one component at a time, several seeds per variant, report mean and spread; what an ablation can and cannot show about why a model works.
M17.5.domain: ENG · Machine learning and deep learning

M17.12.teach: Label audit: sample-and-review, inter-annotator agreement, model-assisted search for likely label errors; how label noise caps and biases the measured accuracy.
M17.12.domain: ENG · Machine learning and deep learning

M18.7.teach: Seeds and variance in RL results: 5-10 or more seeds, confidence intervals across runs, why single-seed learning curves mislead, and reporting practice.

M19.10.teach: Ground truth for evaluating localization: motion capture, RTK-GNSS or surveyed markers; absolute and relative trajectory error (ATE/RPE) and alignment before comparison.
Camera-IMU calibration: intrinsics, extrinsic rotation and translation and time offset (Kalibr-type procedure); verifying it by reprojection error and by VIO drift on a known loop.

M27.1.teach: INCOSE Systems Engineering Competency Framework (SECF): competency areas and proficiency levels; a self-assessment backed by evidence from the learner's own work, repeated as the course advances.

M13.15.n: Rules of thumb and their origin
M13.15.teach: Rules of thumb with provenance: for each rule the derivation or data behind it, the regime where it holds and its typical error; a rule without a source is treated as a hypothesis.

M27.5.n: Dated forecast log scored against outcomes (Brier, error ratio)
M27.5.teach: Personal forecast log: dated numerical predictions with probabilities or ranges, scored later by Brier score and by the log error ratio of estimates; a calibration plot reviewed periodically.
M27.5.he: רשומת תחזיות מתוארכת מול אמת (Brier, יחס שגיאה)

M22.8.teach: Roofline model: arithmetic intensity (FLOP per byte), memory-bound versus compute-bound kernels, reading a roofline plot for a CPU or GPU, and what it predicts for FFT, matrix multiply and convolution.
M22.8.domain: ENG · Periphery: discrete math, algorithms, computer systems, chips

M10.9.teach: Reviewing code changes: reading a diff, what to check (tests, edge cases, numerical changes, silent behavior changes), and reviewing agent-written patches before accepting them.
M10.9.domain: ENG · Periphery: discrete math, algorithms, computer systems, chips

M22.7.teach: Profiling before optimizing: where time and memory go (cProfile or line profiler, perf), cache-miss counters, and checking a speed-up claim with a reproducible benchmark.
M22.7.domain: ENG · Periphery: discrete math, algorithms, computer systems, chips

M0.6.teach: Cramer-Rao bound for signal parameters (time delay, frequency, angle of arrival): Fisher information, the bound sigma about resolution/sqrt(2 SNR), efficiency of the maximum-likelihood estimator, and how the bound feeds DOP-weighted position error and CEP (Kay vol. I ch. 3).

M0.1.n: Every function checked against a numerical example from the books (PoMR, EW101, Kaplan)
M0.1.teach: Checked calculation library: every formula used in the course is implemented once and validated against worked numerical examples in the source books (PoMR, EW 101, Kaplan) before it is used in an analysis.
M0.1.he: כל פונקציה מול דוגמה מספרית מהספר (PoMR, EW101, Kaplan)

M0.1.teach: Continuous integration for the calculation library: the book-example tests run automatically on every change, so a broken formula is caught before it reaches an analysis.

M1.2.teach: Mutual coupling in arrays: self and mutual impedance, active element pattern and active reflection coefficient, scan blindness, and why array calibration must include coupling (Balanis 8.6).
Rectangular microstrip patch: transmission-line and cavity models, resonant length, input impedance and bandwidth versus substrate (Balanis 14.1-14.2), as a closed-form check on simulated patches.
Electromagnetic simulation hygiene: refine the mesh until gain, pattern and S11 change less than a stated tolerance, and check the solver against the analytic dipole and patch before trusting it.

M1.1.teach: Dipole radiation derived: from the infinitesimal dipole to the half-wave dipole, far fields, radiation resistance and directivity (Balanis 4.1-4.6), used as the reference case for checking any antenna computation.
Antenna pattern measurement: far-field distance 2D^2/lambda, anechoic chamber versus outdoor range, reference-antenna gain transfer, and comparison of measured and computed patterns.

M2.4.teach: Calibration with a trihedral corner reflector: sigma = 4 pi a^4 / (3 lambda^2), placement and multipath, and using it to close the radar equation end to end (measured versus predicted SNR).

M2.2.teach: Validation against known objects: calibration spheres, and cooperative aircraft whose position is known from ADS-B; compare measured SNR and position with the prediction.

Cross-tool check of a radar budget: the course's own calculation versus a second independent implementation (e.g., a MATLAB Radar Toolbox example or a published calculator), with differences traced to losses and conventions.

M2.10.teach: Simulation versus measurement of detection performance: measured false-alarm rate on recorded noise and clutter versus the design Pfa, and measured Pd versus SNR against the Swerling curves.

M3.10.teach: Field measurement of detection and identification range: target-to-background temperature difference with a radiometric camera, logged atmosphere (humidity, visibility), and comparison with the range-performance model.

M4.2.teach: Cable bench with known signals: signal generator through attenuators into the receiver; verify sensitivity, dynamic range and parameter measurement (frequency, PRI, pulse width) against the known emitter settings.
M4.2.domain: MIL · Electronic warfare and electromagnetic spectrum operations

M4.3.teach: Open datasets for spectrum processing (e.g., RadioML, public pulse and ADS-B recordings): test deinterleaving and classification code on data the learner did not generate.
M4.3.domain: MIL · Electronic warfare and electromagnetic spectrum operations

M7.9.teach: Mobile ad hoc network routing: link-state versus distance-vector, proactive (OLSR, DSDV) versus reactive (AODV) protocols, CSMA/CA medium access; control overhead, route-repair latency and throughput versus hop count and mobility (Kurose & Ross 5.2, 7.3; Murthy & Manoj 7).

M1.4.teach: Measured link against the predicted budget: received power and SNR versus the Friis and two-ray predictions, with every loss and margin accounted for.

M9.5.teach: SDR measurement of a datalink: received power, SNR or EVM and packet error rate versus range or attenuation, compared with the link budget.

M5.6.teach: Using IGS station data: RINEX observation and navigation files, precise orbits and clocks, and computing one's own position solution for a station with known coordinates to measure the error.
Side-by-side receiver comparison on one antenna through a splitter: C/N0, fix availability, position scatter and time to first fix.

M5.4.teach: Software-receiver processing of recorded GNSS IQ samples (GNSS-SDR-type): acquisition and tracking on a file, checking C/N0 estimates and loop lock indicators against the theory.

M6.4.teach: Zarchan's linearized engagement model as a check: reproduce his normalized miss-distance results for heading error and target acceleration versus flight time over guidance time constant (Zarchan 2-3, 8).
M6.4.domain: MIL · Missiles: propulsion, guidance, control and design

M6.6.teach: Adjoint miss-distance results checked against a Monte Carlo of the nonlinear engagement: where linearization holds and where saturation or large heading errors break it.
M6.6.domain: MIL · Missiles: propulsion, guidance, control and design

M13.4.teach: TLEs and SGP4: propagate a public TLE, compare the predicted pass or position with an observation (visual pass, radio beacon Doppler or published ephemeris), and measure how the error grows with TLE age.
M13.4.domain: MIL · Space systems and space warfare

M9.6.teach: Flight test of a small multirotor: log endurance, electrical power and link quality, and compare them with the hover-power model and the link budget.

M9.7.teach: Measurement data on small drones: published RCS and micro-Doppler campaigns and RF-emission captures; reading the measurement conditions (band, aspect, polarization) before using a number.

M11.4.teach: From delivery accuracy to probability of effect: circular normal miss distribution, R_CEP = 1.1774 sigma, P(miss distance < R) = 1 - exp(-R^2 / (2 sigma^2)); cookie-cutter versus smooth damage functions; partial damage (Przemieniecki 3.11-3.16).
M11.4.domain: MIL · Weapons effects, lethality and protection

M11.4.teach: Effective area of a fragmenting warhead as a computation: fragment spray density, probability of effect given a fragment hit, integration to an effective area, and its use with delivery error (Driels, Weaponeering; JMEM method).
M11.4.domain: MIL · Weapons effects, lethality and protection

M10.5.teach: Checking the salvo model against open data: the public 2023-24 Red Sea engagement record (salvo sizes, intercepts, interceptor types) versus Hughes-model predictions, with the data's gaps stated.

M12.1.n: Terms checked against a military dictionary
M12.1.teach: Terminology discipline: check every term against the official glossaries (ATP 7-100 series glossary, DoD Dictionary) and the original-language term, and note where translations differ in meaning.
M12.1.domain: MIL · Adversary systems, doctrine and capability assessment

M14.4.teach: Source discipline: open and read every cited source, record the exact page or timestamp, confirm the claim is actually in it, and catch citation laundering and AI-invented references.
M14.4.domain: MIL · Defense analysis craft: OSINT, claims checking and communication

M14.4.teach: Independent double geolocation: two analysts or two methods geolocate the same item separately, then compare; disagreement is resolved with new evidence, and the confidence is recorded.
M14.4.domain: MIL · Defense analysis craft: OSINT, claims checking and communication
